properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/02/2025 to WINFALL ENERGY INC N V in Oklahoma Borough, Westmoreland county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/02/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8251227
Permit API: 129-26172
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Oklahoma Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/02/2025
Comments: On October 2 2025, the Department conducted a complaint inspection in regards to CTS 392648. This gas well is currently under an Order (Enf ID 442909). This inspection is not evaluating the operator's compliance with the Order and is being conducted in response to the aforementioned complaint.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the access road and well site appeared to be stabilized with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head and a well posting was present on a piece of the production equipment. There were no observed fluid leaks observed coming from the well head.Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed piping which ran to/from the production tank and the valve near the bottom of the tank, both of which appeared to be heavily corroded. It appeared a small about of fluid was seeping from the corroded portions of the piping onto the ground. The Department obtained a conductivity reading of the fluid on the pipe of 3.07mS. The Department obtained conductivity readings in the gravel below the corroded piping of 1.73ms and 0.87ms in an approximately 1 foot radius from the valve at the bottom of the production tank. These readings appear elevated in comparison to the Department's background conductivity reading of 0.22mS, indicating a release of production fluids has/is occurring.Prior to leaving the site, the Department attempted to contact the operator by calling the phone number on the well tag. The Department's call was sent to voicemail, and the Department was unable to leave a voicemail as the voicemail inbox was full.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed corroded production piping, as well as the observed release.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/15/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8253000
Permit API: 117-20505
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Charleston Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/15/2025
Comments: On 10/15/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Vandergrift 290 well site located in Charleston Twp, Tioga Co. It was 49 degrees and overcast when I arrived on site. Rainfall had impacted the region in the last 24 hours.Prior to this inspection, Seneca personnel had told me that a construction crew was being mobilized to the site to restore the pad back to well pad condition, repairing the spots that were excavated after the release discovered on 5/13/2025. When I arrived on site I did witness some construction equipment at the site. The area that was excavated around and north of the well cellars remains open along with the areas on the fill slope and across the grassy field north of the pad. A Gas Field Specialist crew was on site digging an 8-foot-deep trench across the pad north of the well cellars. Short, downward sloping trenches from each well cellar would be installed to the long trench and then layered with gravel. Clean out pipes will be installed on the east and west end of the long trench with another one in the center. Liquids coming from the well cellars could be monitored in this trench and collected if necessary. A different construction company will be repairing the rest of the pad.Field conductivity readings taken during this inspection are as follows: Liquid on the northeast corner of the pad being 1.066 mS conductance or less. Liquid below the west disturbed area on the fill slope being 0.769 mS conductance. Liquid flowing down from the east fill slope disturbed area being 1.212 mS conductance. Liquid in the sump pit at the northwest corner of the location being 1.315 mS conductance. This fluid was being pumped up to the pad surface into a frac tank on the pad. Soil probe readings taken below the rock lined swale on the west side of the pad being 0.501 mS conductance or less.There are four active wells on site staged for production, along with one plugged well and one that is in the process of being plugged. The Vandergrift 290 2H well has a monument with plugged date of 12/4/2024. The 5H well has not been successfully plugged yet. The production tanks and GPUs are staged in secondary containment.Temporary compost filter socks remain installed below the excavated areas.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 399274 and 4029808 for a release of an unknown amount of produced water to the unprotected pad surface, to the unprotected grassy field below the fill slope and flowing offsite during plugging operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Continue monitoring the area for contamination.2. Continue remediation efforts as necessary. 3. Continue collecting fluids that demonstrate elevated conductance.I left the site at 1000 hours.

Comments: On April 24, 2025, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation of LPR Energy's Humberston Unit 1H well located in Henry Clay Township, Fayette County.At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance and in the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan dated for March 21, 2025, however, the Erosion and Sediment Control Plan (E and S) was dated for June 2010 and was not for plugging operations. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 840896
Permit API: 115-20691
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-30
Comments: WQS Gene Rickard and I performed an INCDT inspection of the Mitchell well site regarding a reported release which occurred aroung 0830 on Jan. 30, 2019. The complaint number was 339494. The release was reported to me via Briana Cunningham, WQSS. Other individuals on site were Mike Deming and Mr. Otten of Southwestern Energy Production Co. The weather at the time of inspection was around 15 degrees F and snowing. Wind was gusting. At about 0830 hrs. a tank in the onsite tank battery was being filled from a production fluid tank. The operator allegedly was monitoring the tank level from the hatch nearest the front part of the tank. According to a relayed assessment, the operator thought the tank was positioned not quite level, allowing the fluid level to overflow the back part of the tank, spilling onto the containment area surrounding the battery. The containment was later found to be compromised and allowed water to leave the containment area. SWN notified the Department on 1/30/2019. According to onsite representatives, approximately 5-6 bbls. of produced water were released to containment, then through the compromised liner to the pad surface. Resource Environmental was called in to delineate the impacted area, and has been directing a dewatering action to mitigate the impact until the tank battery can be moved, as the tanks are currently frozen to the ground. The timeframe for moving the tanks to delineate the affected area appears to be over the weekend. While onsite, crews were attempting to locate any tears in containment, which was being hampered by the icy buildup inside the containment. Workers were also mobilizing tankers to dewater the area and tanks in the tank battery in preparation for movement off containment to allow resource to delineate the affected area. The affected area seems to stop about 10' from the berm, according to test pits dug for assessment. The spill will be going to Act 2. SWN Representative Mike Deming said a possible change in protocol from a 6" to a 12" tank freeboard is being considered. Violations are attached.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 844758
Permit API: 003-22404
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-03-15
Comments: On-site inspection conducted in response to a release of 35 gallons impaired water reported under inspection record 2856634. At the time of this inspection, fracturing operations are ongoing. After arriving on-site, the Department contacted operator representative DJ Hardy by phone at 1316. Per Mr. Hardy, a pump failed during the frac and the transfer line overflowed, resulting in a release of 50 bbl frac water with 35 gallons off of containment. It is believed there is a hole in the containment that allowed this impaired water to be released outside of containment although that hole has yet to be identified. The containment was being pumped out this morning. Mr. Hardy did not respond to this release and will therefore have the appropriate Environmental contact call the Department. At 1335, Jim Noon (EQT Environmental Coordinator) contacted the Department by phone. Per Mr. Noon: Mr. Noon was at the site earlier this morning when the fluid was still being removed from the containment. The release occurred when a discharge hose froze, causing the blunder to overflow frac slurry onto containment before the water transfer could be shut down. It is possible the frac slurry traveled off of containment due to a hole in the containment or a tear in one of the seams; neither have been located at this time. The 35 gallons quantity provided was based off the quantity left in the line and also a visual estimation. Operator representative Darin Sweeney showed the Department where the release occurred. It appears that residual frac slurry/impaired water remains on the containment and also off of containment, notably on the outside edges of the containment. The Department recommends the operator remove all contaminated materials as soon as possible and continue implementing the PPC plan as outlined. Violations are being issued for this reportable release.

Comments: On March 5, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4151444.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. Stage of plugging operations was not confirmed during this inspection.RCE is not installed as depicted on the E and S plan. Surface/vegetation disturbance beyond the width of the access road remains near the entrance as observed in IR 4151444. Plastic matting on access road remains in the same two areas (Photos 7-10).CFS is observed along the access road only on either side of the road at the pre-existing culvert (Photos 11-16). Both sections of CFS are not installed properly as stakes are missing and/or are separated by 10 or more feet between stakes. The CFS on the culvert's outlet side is currently overtopping and causing an erosion channel to begin to form downslope of the CFS. Sediment is not observed to be discharging into the Waters of the Commonwealth at this time.Production tank is observed contained within an adequately vegetated earthen berm. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at the production tank at this time. Pooling of stormwater is observed along the access road closer to the site (Photos 22-23). This water is observed to be exiting the access road and causing an erosion channel to begin to form downslope. No CFS is observed at this area.CFS is observed to be present along the downslope side of the well site as depicted in the E and S plan, however it is not properly installed as stakes are missing and/or are separated by 10 or more feet between stakes (Photos 24-25). Water is currently pooling along the CFS at an area where the stakes have been removed from the surface.The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator maintain all BMPs on-site and install additional controls where necessary, as per the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator seed and mulch or otherwise temporarily stabilize the affected areas of erosion.Violations are continued for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan and for improperly installed CFS.New violations are being issued for erosion and sedimentation and additional sections of improperly installed CFS.

Based on today's inspection, violation remain outstanding as a notice of intent to conduct Act 2 remediation has not yet been received by the Department.

Inspection Date: 1/09/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Seneca Resource's Hepler D 235 well site located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 1/9/2023 at 1030 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of diesel fuel reported by Seneca Resources. Complaint tracking system (CTS) identification # 369178 is tied to this release within CTS. A diesel powered glycol heater had a pinhole leak in a fuel line that caused diesel fuel to release to an interior secondary containment which also had a leak, releasing diesel fuel to a secondary containment structure beneath the entire unit. The secondary containment structure on the ground was discovered to be leaking, which released a mixture of diesel fuel and stormwater to the ground surface. While onsite, company personnel evaluated the impacted area and determined the release to be estimated at 35 gallons of diesel fuel mixed with stormwater from the containment. Crew began by recovering all of the diesel on the surface with a portable vacuum unit. The glycol heater was then transferred to a new, functional secondary containment outside of the impacted area. Once a residual waste container arrived onsite, excavation of the impacted area began. A Seneca representative stated later that 1.5 to 2 inches of pad material was scraped from the impacted area. All impacted material was placed into a lined residual waste container for later disposal. Excavation and remedial activities were completed by 1300 hours on 1/9/2023. The glycol heater unit was repaired and it's secondary containment was replaced. No portion of the diesel fuel release was able to escape the pad surface.Based on the findings of this inspection report, the reported release made by Seneca Resources, and the timely remediation completed by the operator, violations of the following are cited against API #117-21531 as immediately corrected:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)I departed the site at 1130 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 951622
Permit API: 059-25016
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Washington Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/06/2022
Comments: On 4/6/22 an incident inspection of the Pettit GH84 OG Well site was conducted in response to a report of spill received by the Department on 4/4/22. Initial details of the spill were reported by CNX at approximately 5:30pm on 4/4/22. The report stated that at approximately 3:30pm on 4/4/22 a leak was discovered around the valve of buried waterline at the GH84 well site. It was estimated that two barrels of brine were released. On 4/6/22 at approximately 8:45am, I called Kyle Borden of CNX to inquire about the spill. He stated that a leak was discovered in a buried three-inch polyline leading from the GH84 coalbed methane well to a tank battery. The leak was discovered by the lease operator during a routine inspection on 4/4/22. The well had previously been inspected on 3/30/22 and no leak was observed at that time. The lease operator observed an orange/red fluid saturating the ground behind the well pumpjack. The well was shut in upon discovery of the leak. Mr. Borden stated that excavation of the area began on 4/5/22. Due to overnight precipitation, the excavated area needed pumped the morning of 4/6/22. Mr. Borden stated that SPSI was contracted for remediation and Penn E&R was contracted for sampling. During the site inspection, the following was observed: -A crew was on-site excavating impacted substrate from the spill area (Photos #1-3 and #8). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the area that was actively being remediated. -BMPs were observed downslope of the disturbed area (Photos #5-6). -The area below the installed BMPs (Photo #7) did not exhibit elevated conductivity. -A well sign was posted at the pumpjack (Photo #9). Mr. Borden stated that after the initial remediation efforts, following the overnight precipitation, elevated conductivity was observed in the area that had been excavated. Upon further remediation of the area, Mr. Borden estimated that five barrels of brine were released. CNX plans to continue excavation of impacted material until elevated conductivity is no longer detected. An additional roll-off container was in route to the site at the time of the inspection. Mr. Borden stated that four roll-off boxes had already been filled and removed from the site. CNX is following Act 2 protocol for the spill. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, and 78.54 are being issued for the release.

Comments: On 04/09/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 42 degrees and sunny. Water Quality Specialist Korey Starkey and I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP traveled the area of the impact beginning at the release point (CTS #396090) (photo #2). The DEP was unable to field measure the Electrical Conductivity (EC) at the release point due to stimulation activities. The EC of the fluids up-gradient of the stormwater basin were ~ 240 us/cm (photo #3). The stormwater basin with containment has one 24/7 water truck recovering fluids on top of and underneath the containment and from the sumps. The EC of the fluids on top of the containment were ~ 277 us/cm (photo #4). The EC of the fluids in the sump located down gradient of where overflow pipe was located were ~ 742 us/cm (photo #6). Temporary E and S controls have been installed down gradient of the stormwater basin (photo #6). The EC of the soil down gradient of the stormwater basin was ~4.0 mS/cm. On 04/03/2026 an additional sump was installed further down gradient (photo #9). The additional sump is manned 24/7. Fluids are recovered from the sump ~ every hour. The EC of the fluids in the additional sump were ~1.4 mS/cm (1400 us/cm) (photo #10). The EC of fluids down gradient of the additional sump were between 101-104 us/cm. At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-529) UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the discharge the EC of the fluids were 71 us/cm (photo #13). The EC of the fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the confluence were ~ 935 us/cm (photo #14). At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-530) from UNT Rockwell Creek downstream of the discharge the EC of fluids were ~160 us/cm. As of 04/06/2026 5,293 barrels (166,729 gallons) have been recovered onsite. Resource management will continue screening and sampling ten monitoring points twice a week. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for EC between 430-640 us/cm. There was no evidence of any additional spills or releases. Proper secondary containment was observed throughout the site. Stimulation activities are to be continued until 04/30/2026.Violations remain open against API #015-23994. We departed at 1115 hours.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8270051
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/09/2026
Comments: On 04/09/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 42 degrees and sunny. Water Quality Specialist Korey Starkey and I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP traveled the area of the impact beginning at the release point (CTS #396090) (photo #2). The DEP was unable to field measure the Electrical Conductivity (EC) at the release point due to stimulation activities. The EC of the fluids up-gradient of the stormwater basin were ~ 240 us/cm (photo #3). The stormwater basin with containment has one 24/7 water truck recovering fluids on top of and underneath the containment and from the sumps. The EC of the fluids on top of the containment were ~ 277 us/cm (photo #4). The EC of the fluids in the sump located down gradient of where overflow pipe was located were ~ 742 us/cm (photo #6). Temporary E and S controls have been installed down gradient of the stormwater basin (photo #6). The EC of the soil down gradient of the stormwater basin was ~4.0 mS/cm. On 04/03/2026 an additional sump was installed further down gradient (photo #9). The additional sump is manned 24/7. Fluids are recovered from the sump ~ every hour. The EC of the fluids in the additional sump were ~1.4 mS/cm (1400 us/cm) (photo #10). The EC of fluids down gradient of the additional sump were between 101-104 us/cm. At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-529) UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the discharge the EC of the fluids were 71 us/cm (photo #13). The EC of the fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the confluence were ~ 935 us/cm (photo #14). At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-530) from UNT Rockwell Creek downstream of the discharge the EC of fluids were ~160 us/cm. As of 04/06/2026 5,293 barrels (166,729 gallons) have been recovered onsite. Resource management will continue screening and sampling ten monitoring points twice a week. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for EC between 430-640 us/cm. There was no evidence of any additional spills or releases. Proper secondary containment was observed throughout the site. Inspection Date: 2020-01-10
Comments: As documented in Inspection Record #2971125, the self-reported amount of oil-based mud released was 5 barrels (see Spill/Release Information of Photo #2). The Department recommended remediating the spill pursuant to §78a66(c)2 in an Inspection received by the operator on December 13, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, a satisfactory initial written report pursuant to §78a66(c)2 has not been received. The report provided by the operator on December 12, 2019 and documented in Inspection Record #2971125 only satisfies §78a66(c)2(i)(A), (C), and (F). Inspection Records #2970703 and #2971139 shows petroleum-based mud in multiple locations on the pad. Inspection Record #2971139 shows an unknown substance with a rainbow sheen discharging from under secondary containment at least 100 feet from the well heads. The Department collected multiple sample on the site on December 6, 2019. Sample results show the petroleum-based mud in an erosion rill greater than 200 feet from the well heads. The rill is on the edge of the well pad and discharges toward a stormwater channel which leads to the PCSM forebay; this evidence is sufficient to not only show the extent of the spill, but also that the spilled material has left the well pad and entered stormwater facilities. Per a telephone conversation with Chevron representative B. A. Lambie on January 8, 2020, the initial remediation by Chevron was completed on December 9, 2019. Department personnel were on-site on December 9, 2019 as documented in Inspection Record #298131. At the time of inspection, secondary containment was still in place. A strong petroleum odor and non-bacterial sheen were observed near and in stormwater channel R-4, respectively. The Department collected multiple samples from the site on December 27, 2019. The rill and nearby areas had not been altered as of December 27, 2019, nor had channel R-4. Sample results from December 27, 2019 show hexane is present in at least three locations in the material spilled near the pad entrance as mentioned in Inspection Record #2970703. The spilled material will need remediated pursuant to §78a66(c). At this time, hexane is being treated as a separate spill. Additional violations are being issued. Photographs are referenced as part of the operator-provided inspections provided on December 16, 2019 as requested in Inspection Record #2971139. However, the photographs cannot be accessed. Therefore, the inspections provided were incomplete. The photographs were requested via e-mail on December 17, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, the photographs have not been provided. Additional violations may be forthcoming based on review of the complete inspections. In Inspection Record #2971139, the Department requested photographic documentation of the removal of the secondary containment that remained on December 6, 2019 be provided by December 27, 2019. As of January 10, 2019, the documentation has not been provided.

Comments: Narrative: On 8 June 2020, Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (Department) Water Quality Specialist Mark Madeley (Madeley) and Water Quality Specialist Supervisor Rich Sheriff (Sheriff) conducted a routine/complete inspection (inspection) of the Oakland 11 OG Well (well) in order to determine compliance with the Oil and Gas Act and the applicable technical regulations in 25 Pa. Code Chapters 78 & 102. The following was observed during the Department's inspection: 1. The well was stable and producing, with the pit having been previously reclaimed. The 23 December 2019 inspection of the site indicated that the area was, ‘snow covered and stable…appeared that temporary stabilisation measures will need to be used when weather allows'. 2. Madeley and Sheriff observed a lack of uniform vegetative cover at the site - with no evidence of seed or mulch having been placed. The pit appeared to have deformities as well and was not shaped in such a way as to prevent the pooling of water. 3. Madeley and Sheriff noted the presence of a well permit attached to a nearby tree but no evidence of a site tag on the pump jack or wellhead. 4. Mr James Highhouse arrived on-site during the inspection and told Sheriff and Madeley that he was going to immediately lay mulch about the area. Mr Highhouse also made reference to the presence of a mini-excavator already near the site and said he would be using the machine to grade the pit area for better stabilisation. 5. Sheriff and Madeley expressed their intention to have a look at other wells in the area whilst inspecting and Mr Highhouse said he would be attaching site tags to the Oakland 11 and other nearby pump jacks immediately. Madeley and Sheriff observed Mr Highhouse attaching signs to the Oakland 11 and Oakland 12 (123-48277) pump jacks. The Department has reviewed the observations of Madeley and requests the following information be submitted prior to 17 July 2020: 1. Evidence confirming the pit area has been better shaped to resist pooling of water and erosion See below under REMARKS/VIOLATIONS: PA Code Title 25, Chapter 78.53 & 102.4 (b) (1) and PA Code Title 58, Oil & Gas Act, Chapter 32, 3216 (b): During and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including…producing…the operator shall design, implement and maintain best management practises; [T]he following erosion and sediment control requirements apply…implementation and maintenance of E&S BMPs are required to minimise the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation 2. Evidence confirming mulch has been spread about the area in order to facilitate further vegetative reclamation which will lead to >70% uniform vegetative cover See below under REMARKS/VIOLATIONS: PA Code Title 25, 102.22: Permanent stabilisation. Upon final completion of an earth disturbance activity…top-soil restored, replaced, or amended, seeded, mulched or otherwise permanently stabilised and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation; Clean Streams Law, Section 402 (b) The requested documentation can be faxed to my attention at 814 723 0964, sent via e-mail to mamadeley@pa.gov or posted to the following address: ¿Mark Madeley ¿DEP- Bureau of District Oil and Gas Operations ¿Northwest District -Warren Office ¿321 North State Street ¿Warren, PA 16365 If you have any questions, please contact Mark Madeley at 814 308 3118. On 15 June 2020, a copy of this narrative was sent (in SAIR application) via e-mail to JRHOIL69@msn.com, afterwards Madeley also phoned Mr Highhouse at 814 688 1443

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Columbia and Springfield Townships, Bradford County on 7/21/2025 at 0920 hours. The weather was 65 degrees F with cloudy skies.Remediation efforts are currently underway. A large pit has been excavated around the 7H well (photo #12) and the impacted material is piled onsite for later removal/disposal (photo #14). Repsol plans to have the wellhead reconstructed and then remedial efforts downslope will begin. The extent of downslope impacts off the western corner of the well pad and along the surface waterline in the adjacent field have been delineated. A temporary berm has been installed in the adjacent field, downslope of impacts, to collect fluids as runoff from precipitation occurs (photo #5). The surface waterline has been removed from the impacted area and from the constructed "corner" berm. Numerous areas of distressed vegetation were observed during this inspection (photos #2, 4, 8, 10 and 11).Resource Environmental (Resource), alongside Repsol's construction contractor, began screening and excavating impacted pad material and soils on Friday, 7/18/2025. Repsol reported that all material field measured at >1.0mS/cm is being recovered and stored for later disposal. Material recovered is being placed into lined residual waste containers which are then being covered prior to site departure. Repsol reported that three trucks are running today for removal of the residual waste containers as they are filled. Resource is screening material/soils every few feet, horizontally and vertically, to guide the excavation efforts.Repsol has Larson Design Group working on designing a more permanent type of land design downslope of the pad in order to continue the collection and recovery of fluids. Repsol plans to have a lined sump constructed within the temporary "corner" berm to continue collecting and recovering fluids. A "supervac" water truck is scheduled to arrive tomorrow morning to finish recovering all of the fluids held within the post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) basin. The DEP recommends the following:-continuing fluids and impacted soils recovery-continuing monitoring nearby streams for potential impacts-continuing soil screening/monitoring to determine the extent of the impacts offsiteViolations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301The DEP departed the site at 1100 hours.

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8178618
Permit API: 129-26206
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/06/2024
Comments: On March 6, 2024, inspection conducted in response to a complaint (CTS-374226) on the Terence Shaffer 1-P041 well in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The following was observed:The well site was flooded by rainwater at the time of inspection (see photos 4 and 13). This did not appear to result in sedimentation on the well site during the time of inspection. The well site exhibited less than 70 percent vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. A gas odor was detected onsite. Hissing and bubbling was observed coming from the well head (see photos 2 and 3). The well API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 6). However, the onsite posting lacked the operator's address. Little to no vegetative growth coverage was observed on the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 7 and 8). A cotton-like substance was observed stuffed into one of the brine tank valves, with water flowing out of this valve (see photo 9). No elevated conductivity readings were detected underneath either brine tank valve, or anywhere onsite (see photos 5, 11, 12, and 14). Tire rutting that was severely eroded to bare stone was observed in the access road entrance (see photo 15). Sediment-laden pooling was observed in these ruts at a low point in the access road (see photo 16). An apparent stream or tributary flows through a culvert underneath this point in the access road. This sediment-laden pooling could be observed flowing from the access road ruts into this apparent stream/tributary at the culvert outlet, resulting in a discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photos 17 and 18). Department vehicles were not used to access the well site or access road for this inspection.The Department recommends that the operator post their address onsite, as is required by current regulations. OGI follow-up is being requested for evaluation of well integrity.Violations are being issued against the brine tank onsite, as it appears that it would fail to keep production fluids contained. Additional violations are being issued for failing to permanently stabilize the well site and access road, resulting in a sediment-laden discharge to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: The DEP conducted a restoration inspection of Chesapeake's Stone well site located in Tuscarora Township, Bradford County on 6/23/2021 at 1150 hours. The weather was 64 degrees with partly cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a post-drilling well site restoration report submitted by Chesapeake. There are four active wells on location, two of which were recently hydraulically fractured and remain under flow-back conditions. The site remains permanently stabilized through vegetative cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed during the inspection. Post-construction stormwater management controls are in place and remain functional at this time. Containment structures are intact and no leaks or other integrity issues were identified. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed during the inspection. Violations cited against API # 015-23632 on 2/1/2021 for a produced water release will remain OUTSTANDING at this time. Upon attainment of Act 2 standards, the violations could then be closed out. Based on the findings of today's inspection, the post-drilling well site restoration report will be approved. No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1230 hours.

Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/04/2024
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8182288
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/04/2024
Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.
